newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police enter Northern League HQ.
newsitem.headline: Italian police enter Northern League HQ.

text.p: Police searching for evidence of alleged anti-constitutional activities entered the headquarters of Italy's separatist Northern League party on Wednesday after an hours-long stand-off, reporters and League officials said.

They said detectives entered the reception area of the building in Milan and then forced aside three League members of parliament, including former interior minister Roberto Maroni, who had tried to block their access to offices.
The police had spent several hours outside the building, where Maroni and other senior League officials had contested the validity of a search warrant.

The warrant was among several issued by a prosecutor in the northern town of Verona who is investigating alleged criminal attempts to undermine the unity of the state by three organisers of the League's self-styled "green shirt" security squad.

League offices elsewhere and homes of members were also searched on Wednesday. Calls for criminal action against the League have grown since its leader Umberto Bossi proclaimed a northern "republic of Padania" in Venice on Sunday.
The Italian news agency AGI reported from the League headquarters that police had given Maroni and the other two parliamentarians three warnings before pushing past them.
